column3: The Hebrew says earth was upon them without explicitly naming their heads; BSB specifies dust on their heads.
The Hebrew calls Israel’s descendants its seed and the foreigners sons of a foreigner; BSB says Israelite descent and foreigners.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls it the ascent of the Levites; BSB says a raised platform.
The Hebrew uses an active plural blessing of the name of Your glory; BSB uses the passive “Blessed be Your glorious name.”
The Hebrew says the heavens of the heavens; BSB says the highest heavens.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew speaks of upholding Your words in the plural; BSB says keeping Your promise in the singular.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls Pharaoh’s personnel servants and refers to the victims by a pronoun; BSB says officials and explicitly names our fathers.
The Hebrew repeats the sea for their crossing; BSB uses “it” for the second reference.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives law in the singular and uses the image of Moses’ hand; BSB gives laws in the plural and says through Moses.
The Hebrew says You lifted Your hand to give them the land; BSB expresses this as swearing to give it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew places their return to bondage “in their rebellion”; BSB says “in Egypt.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the cloud pillar did not depart from above them; BSB describes it as never turning away from guiding them.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately names the land of Sihon and the land of the king of Heshbon; BSB combines them as the land of Sihon king of Heshbon.
The Hebrew calls their descendants sons; BSB says descendants.
The Hebrew calls the entrants sons; BSB says descendants. It uses hand in the singular; BSB uses hands in the plural.
The Hebrew describes the land as fat and the wells as hewn; BSB says fertile land and wells already dug.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the root of distress for the enemies and their oppression; BSB says enemies who oppressed them.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they gave a rebellious shoulder, in the singular; BSB says they stubbornly shrugged their shoulders.

The Hebrew makes You the subject of admonishing through Your Spirit and the hand of Your prophets; BSB makes Your Spirit the subject. The Hebrew says peoples of the lands; BSB says neighboring peoples.
